tagline: Beneath the Sierra Nevada, Granada is crowned by the Alhambra, the most famous Moorish palace in the world, with the hillside Albaicín quarter and free tapas with every drink.
overview: Granada was the last Muslim kingdom in Spain, surrendering to Ferdinand and Isabella in 1492. Its rulers left the Alhambra, a hilltop fortress and palace complex of carved stucco, tiled halls and fountains, and the Generalife gardens beside it. Together with the Albaicín it is a UNESCO site.

The Albaicín, the old Moorish quarter, climbs the hill opposite in a maze of white houses and lanes; the Mirador de San Nicolás has the classic view of the Alhambra with the snowy Sierra Nevada behind. Sacromonte's cave houses are known for flamenco.

Ferdinand and Isabella are buried in the Royal Chapel beside the cathedral. Granada is a student city and one of the last places in Spain where a free tapa comes with every drink, and the Sierra Nevada ski resort is under an hour away.
